system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

  PROVISIONAL DIRECTION — set by leadership before this review

    The provisional direction for this cycle is simplify_onboarding. It is
    not final: you may confirm it or replace it with any other candidate.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  1 inherited memory before committing. Name it by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memory you want verified (up to one, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: Two of the six inherited memories (memory_86, memory_31) point at onboarding/signup simplification, and they line up with the two metrics that are actually degrading internally: onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%). Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single fix there plausibly addresses both symptoms, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats only the downstream one. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting response to the competitor, but discount-led SMB acquisition buys volume at the cost of margin and cohort quality, which cuts against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; it is also a reactive move on the competitor's chosen terrain. Referral (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are sound but address neither of the deteriorating metrics this week. I am spending the single verification on memory_86 rather than on a rival candidate because it is the load-bearing and most recent evidence for the provisional direction, and it is the claim whose exact wording worries me: it reports completion rates, time-to-value and 'early product adoption' but says nothing about revenue or retention. If the archived record shows the lift was measured only as funnel completion, or decayed after the first week, then the provisional direction is resting on a vanity metric and I would fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91, most recent overall, directly targets the larger 6% drop). Verifying memory_73 instead would be lower value: even a strong promo-pricing record would not change my read that discount-driven SMB acquisition is the wrong instrument for a long-term qualified-revenue objective, so that verification could not flip the decision. Confirming for now, contingent on what the archive returns.
